title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Tale of the Bloody Benders
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with Jerry) cover the Bloody Benders, a family of murderers who ran a tavern and homestead along the Osage Trail near Cherryvale, Kansas, in the 1870s. Topics include the frontier setting and violent backdrop of Kansas, the Bender family members (John Bender Sr. "Pa", John Bender Jr., "Ma" Elvira Bender, and daughter Kate), the murders of travelers in the cellar and creek, the disappearance of Dr. William York and George Longcore and his daughter Mary Anne, the search led by Colonel Alexander York, the discovery of the trapdoor cellar and bodies in the orchard, the vigilante theories and arrests of twelve men, the family's flight and unresolved fate, the reward, later land purchase and investigation, and pop culture references. The episode ends with a listener email and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening and listener suggestion
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Bloody Benders as a Halloween true crime pick, suggested by listener Star White from Kansas who saw Bender signs in Montgomery County.

segments.title: Setting and the Bender family arrival
segments.summary: Kansas in the 1870s as frontier after the Osage removal. John Bender Sr. (Pa), John Bender Jr. (sometimes alias John Gebhart), and Ma Elvira Bender arrive; daughter Kate and her spiritualist flyers are described. The family runs a tavern and orchard near the Osage Trail.

segments.title: The tavern and early murders
segments.summary: Description of the small tavern with a canvas divider, the family's reputation in the community, and the Ali's-style goods sold there. Hosts explain the violent Kansas backdrop, and the discovery of murdered men in Drum Creek, including William Jones carrying about $250.

segments.title: Escaped woman and suspicions
segments.summary: In February 1873 a woman who stopped at the house escaped barefoot after seeing weapons on a table and Ma Bender's remark about supper. The family's reputation grows as violently unusual.

segments.title: Disappearance of George Longcore and Dr. William York
segments.summary: George Longcore and his daughter Mary Anne vanish on the way to Iowa. Neighbor Dr. William York investigates, finds abandoned wagon near Fort Scott, and then disappears. Colonel Alexander York, a Civil War colonel and Kansas senator, leads a search party of about seventy-five men.

segments.title: Town search and the Benders' flight
segments.summary: The search party visits the Bender home, where Ma claims to speak no English and John Jr. shows bullet marks. Ma later accuses the escaped woman of being a witch. A town meeting leads to a search, but the Benders have fled by train, leaving their horse, wagon and dog behind.

segments.title: Cellar discovery and bodies
segments.summary: Volunteers find a trapdoor and a blood-soaked stone cellar that smells of decay. Bodies are found in the orchard, a well and along with Mary Anne, with about eleven found and the total linked to as many as twenty-one murders. The curtain seating and the murder method are described.

segments.title: Victims' accounts, dark tourism and vigilante arrests
segments.summary: Witnesses who narrowly escaped describe the curtain seating. Visitors looted the house. Hosts note the Bender murders as early American serial killings. Twelve men are arrested as alleged accomplices, and a vigilante group called the Regulators is connected through the posed bodies.

segments.title: Identities, fate, reward and legends
segments.summary: Modern research suggests Ma was Almira Meek and Kate was Eliza Griffith, with John Sr. possibly John Flickinger. Reports of the family's fate range from suicide to a stroke in New Mexico, and a large reward went unclaimed. Laura Ingalls Wilder family story is described as untrue.

segments.title: Land purchase, pop culture and sources
segments.summary: Bob Miller bought the Bender land and plans investigations with UK or K State. The 2016 movie Bender is mentioned, Red Dead Redemption 2 is said to have been inspired by the family, and a Genealogy Trails website collects original newspaper accounts.

segments.title: Listener mail from Tanya Vanderpool
segments.summary: Listener Tanya Vanderpool shares that she listened to the show while delivering mail and at the dentist, where her dentist was a fan of the Chowchilla bus kidnapping episode. Hosts also chat about Thirty Rock.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and give the show's contact and production information.
